question: Whether in times of crisis or not, Europeans always care about food security and food production. Together with livestock farmers, fruit and vegetable growers, fishers, silviculturists, hunters and foresters, our agricultural holdings provide healthy, safe and affordable food and environmentally friendly raw materials from Europe. They are the beating heart of our countrysides.

However, our farms are under tremendous pressure. The vast majority of customers expect them to offer the best services at the lowest prices, not to mention the competitive pressure they face from non-EU competitors. A level playing field therefore needs to be established for companies across Europe. The framework for this is the EU’s common agricultural policy (CAP).
The CAP should primarily serve European agriculture – this means also ensuring that EU regulations do not to put our farmers at a competitive disadvantage. In view of the above: 1.
Should CAP funds be used predominantly and in a targeted manner to ensure the security and production of food and raw materials?

What is the Commission doing to cut down the red tape around the CAP and make it more targeted, so that our farmers can earn a decent income and receive the protection they need on the highly volatile agricultural markets?

Does it see a need for the current EU Nitrates Directive, among other things, to be revised so that it covers all nitrate inputs in future and provides for a standardised EU-wide network of measuring points?
answer: 1. The Common Agricultural Policy Strategic Plans (CSPs) are the key tool to deliver on the objectives of the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP). They are underpinned by EUR 307 billion of public expenditure for the 2023-2027 period.

The CSPs include targeted strategies to address Member States’ circumstances and needs to contribute to economic, environmental and climate as well as social objectives, thus supporting resilience in the farming sector and rural areas and contributing to food security. 2.

The Commission launched a thorough analysis of the administrative burden weighing on farmers’ shoulders to identify areas for improvement and presented on 22 February 2024 a first set of possible actions to help reduce the administrative burden weighing on farmers’ shoulders (1).

On 7 March 2024 the Commission launched a survey addressed to farmers to understand the burden placed on farmers by procedures and rules linked to CAP financial support as well as other rules for food and agriculture in the EU.

On 15 March 2024, (2) the Commission proposed to review certain provisions of the CAP, related to conditionality and CSPs, with the aim to reduce the burden related to controls for EU small farmers, and provide CAP beneficiaries with greater flexibility for complying with certain environmental conditionalities.

The Commission also prepared a reflection paper outlining measures to improve the position of farmers in the food chain. 3. The evaluation of the Nitrates Directive, announced in the 2024 Commission Work Programme, (3) is ongoing and planned to be finalised in 2025.
An open public consultation finalised on 8 March 2024, resulting in more than 1000 replies from citizens and stakeholders, will also form the basis of analysis in the coming months.
